title: Jeroboam’s calves: Jehu’s zeal for Jehovah coexisted with Bethel and Dan—cult referred to the true God
source_text: XXXI. Eadem fuit ratio cultus vitulis exhibiti a Rege Jeroboam & successoribus ejus. Quod enim in istis vitulis, se Jehovam verum Deum colere professi sint, patet exemplo Jehu: qui cultores omnes Baalis deleturus, gloriabatur de suo erga Jehovam Zelo, sic dicens amico suo Jonadab filio Recab, Veni mecum & vide Zelum meum pro Domino. Et tamen non recessit a peccatis Jeroboam filii Nabat, qui peccare fecit Israel, nec dereliquit vitulos aureos, qui erant in Bethel, & in Dan: Deum, scilicet, non aliter colens, quam in illis imaginibus, quarum proinde cultum referebat ad verum Deum Jehovam. Ut videre est libro 2. Regum cap. 10.
pass_a_gloss: The same was the reason of the cult exhibited to the calves by King Jeroboam and his successors. For that in those calves they professed to cultivate Jehovah the true God is plain from the example of Jehu: who, about to destroy all the cultivators of Baal, gloried in his Zeal toward Jehovah, saying thus to his friend Jonadab son of Recab, Come with me and see my Zeal for the Lord. And yet he did not depart from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin, nor did he forsake the golden calves which were in Bethel, and in Dan: cultivating God, namely, not otherwise than in those images, whose cult accordingly he referred to the true God Jehovah. As is to be seen in the second book of Kings chapter 10.
pass_b_english: Jehu can burn for Jehovah against Baal and still keep Jeroboam’s calves.
Those calves were image-vehicles of Jehovah-cult—relative, and still sinful.

choices.why: Twin cult sites of Jeroboam’s calves.
